newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiffs end opening argument in Fla. smoke case.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiffs end opening argument in Fla. smoke case.

text.p: The attorney pressing a landmark $5 billion secondhand smoke case ended his opening arguments on Monday with a plea that U.S. tobacco companies be severely punished for decades of alleged deceit.
"Lies, fraud, deceit justify punitive damages," plaintiff attorney Stanley Rosenblatt said at the end of 2-1/2 hours of speaking.
Punitive damages are monies assessed beyond the cost of actual injuries to punish a defendant in a civil lawsuit.

Rosenblatt has said he will ask the jury to award in excess of $5 billion in punitive damages in addition to any of the "actual damages" awarded in the suit, known as Norma Broin et al vs Philip Morris Cos Inc et al.

Rosenblatt represents a class of an estimated 60,000 non-smoking flight attendants who claim that their tobacco-related illnesses such as lung cancer were caused by passenger smoke aboard U.S.-based passenger jets before 1988.

He said earlier that he would call two former U.S. surgeon generals and an array of chemists, scientists and statisticians to illustrate his claim that secondhand smoke causes disease and that the tobacco industry lied to Americans about the dangers of smoking.
Attorneys representing seven tobacco companies and two trade groups are scheduled to make their opening arguments on Tuesday.
